Organization is not cosmetic file arrangement. It creates a controlled relationship among accepted source snapshots, preserved source packages, staged representations, derived datasets, schemas, identifiers, transformation records, QA evidence, and analysis-ready objects.

Each staged-dataset record begins as **not ready for analysis**. Its status changes only after the Organize gate has been reviewed. A ready status records the responsible decision-maker and decision time. Every new staged version requires its own readiness decision; superseding a dataset does not silently transfer readiness to its replacement.

## Organize boundary

The Organize stage begins after a snapshot is **accepted for staging** or **accepted with documented limitation**. It may include structural inspection, deterministic transformation, normalization, schema and identifier checks, unit and code harmonization, spatial and temporal standardization, documented exclusions and corrections, provenance records, and analysis-readiness checks.

It does not include statistical model selection, parameter estimation, hypothesis testing, interpretation, predictive-accuracy assessment, model-assumption validation, publication review, or operational release.

## Organize workflow

1. Confirm the accepted snapshot and intake status.
2. Register the working dataset and authoritative locations.
3. Establish project and data-object roles.
4. Preserve the source-to-staged boundary.
5. Transform source data through documented code or procedures.
6. Define identifiers, relationships, schema, units, and codes.
7. Establish spatial and temporal conventions.
8. Run structural and completeness checks.
9. Record limitations and unresolved discrepancies.
10. Approve or withhold analysis readiness.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  accepted[Accepted snapshot] --> preserved[Preserved source package]
  preserved --> transformed[Scripted or documented transformation]
  transformed --> staged[Staged dataset]
  staged --> checks[Schema, identifier, spatial, temporal, and structural checks]
  checks --> ready[Analysis-ready dataset]
  checks -. unresolved .-> hold[Not ready; resolve or document limitation]
```

“Analysis-ready” is a workflow status, not a scientific endorsement. Passing intake allows a snapshot to enter staging. Passing the Organize gate allows a structurally documented dataset to enter Analyze. Neither gate establishes that a statistical method, model, inference, forecast, or scientific conclusion is valid.

## Evidence and interpretation

This draft workflow is informed by the existing [resource catalog](../../resources/index.qmd), including [Good Enough Practices](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00037), [The Turing Way](https://book.the-turing-way.org/), [RDMkit](https://rdmkit.elixir-europe.org/), [DataONE](https://dataone.org/best-practices/), [TIER](https://www.projecttier.org/tier-protocol/), [FAIR Principles](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles/), [FGDC](https://www.fgdc.gov/metadata), [GBIF](https://docs.gbif.org/georeferencing-best-practices/), [CDC guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/data-management.html), [EML](https://knb.ecoinformatics.org/external/), and [EFI](https://ecoforecast.org/). These sources inform practices for separation, scripting, provenance, identity, metadata, spatial and temporal meaning, and reproducibility. Access date: 2026-08-05. External guidance informs this draft workflow but does not establish GeoEpi or institutional policy.

## Analysis-readiness gate

- [ ] The source and accepted snapshot are identifiable.
- [ ] The preserved source package remains distinguishable from staged and derived objects.
- [ ] Staged or derived dataset IDs and versions are assigned.
- [ ] Consequential transformations are scripted or documented.
- [ ] Code, configuration, and transformation records identify how the dataset was produced.
- [ ] Corrections and exclusions are attributable.
- [ ] Record counts and structural checks are plausible.
- [ ] Primary, foreign, composite, spatial, and temporal identifiers are documented as applicable.
- [ ] Duplicate and join behavior has been assessed.
- [ ] Fields, types, units, categories, missingness, and derivations are documented.
- [ ] Spatial reference, support, resolution, alignment, and boundary versions are documented where applicable.
- [ ] Event, report, extraction, acquisition, processing, and aggregation times are distinguishable where applicable.
- [ ] Restrictions and sensitive fields remain correctly handled.
- [ ] Unresolved discrepancies and limitations are visible.
- [ ] An authoritative analysis-ready object and responsible decision-maker are recorded.
- [ ] Dataset status is explicitly recorded as **ready for analysis**, **ready for analysis with documented limitation**, or **not ready for analysis**.

Passing this gate establishes structural and documentary readiness only. Analytical validity, model suitability, inferential validity, predictive performance, and scientific interpretation belong to later stages. A ready status is therefore a workflow decision, not an endorsement of a scientific result.

**Ready for analysis** permits entry to [Analyze](../analyze/index.qmd). **Ready for analysis with documented limitation** permits entry with that limitation carried forward. **Not ready for analysis** does not permit entry. The Analyze stage ends at a future Validate stage; it does not establish that a method, model, prediction, or scientific conclusion is valid.
